title: ci(test-core): re-size the Test Core shard wall 45 -> 40 from the measured post-slicing job walls
body:
Fixes #22075
Clause-②: no

## What this does

Re-sizes the `Test Core` shard job's `timeout-minutes` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` from **45 to 40**, and rewrites the rationale comment above it to carry the measured window, the per-event maxima and the slowest run. This is Done-when clause 3 of the card. One file, comment plus one value; no step, matrix, job name, required context, stall-guard setting or other job's timeout changes.

**Ruling.** The maintainer's answer on the decision `6082946866`, recorded in `6083012192`: 「A 停在 3 片收口 (Recommended)」. Under it `FILE_SHARDED_PACKAGES` stays `{ '@objectstack/cli': 3 }`. Done-when clause 2 (the 1.3 slowest-over-mean ratio on affected-set runs) is withdrawn, and the card is accepted on the measured speed-up. Clause 1 landed with PR #22456 as `5919483472`. This PR is clause 3, so it closes the card.

## The window

The window covers every CI run whose tested tree carries `5919483472`. Read from the jobs API at 2026-10-09T16:20Z.

- **Membership.** For `push`, `schedule` and `merge_group`, the run's head commit must answer `ahead` or `identical` to `GET compare/5919483472...HEAD_SHA`. That is 29 `ahead` and 1 `identical` (the round-3 queue group itself). The control `3ca71b6e05`, its parent, answers `behind`.
- **Pull requests.** For `pull_request`, the run must be created at or after 11:03:23Z, when `main` first carried the commit. A PR run tests the PR merged onto `main` as of that moment.
- **Range.** Runs 37917885267 to 37956350887, created 10:29Z to 16:03Z.
- **Wall.** `completed_at − started_at` of each `Test Core (N/6)` job, on attempt 1. No run in the window was re-run.

- **Failure runs are kept.** Their Test Core jobs ran to a conclusion under the same wall. 37921971792 shard 4/6 failed at 24.9 min, 37930835817 shard 2/6 failed at 19.6 min, and 37931072987 shard 2/6 failed at 20.7 min.
- **Cancelled runs are excluded.** Their jobs are censored by supersession. The largest cancelled job wall is 25.3 min, on 37952087770 `(4/6)`, cancelled 1095 s into its test step. That is below the maximum above.
- **Before the change,** the six heaviest pre-change pull_request runs in the same listing had slowest jobs of 31.7–39.7 min: 37920407075 39.7, 37919214042 38.2, 37918024929 37.6, 37919833209 34.9, 37920676666 34.0, 37920713245 31.7. Each time the slowest was `Test Core (1/6)`, the shard that ran the whole CLI alone.

**Did the CLI run as slices?** I read the aggregate `Test Core` job's timing table on 10 runs. On each, `@objectstack/cli` reads `all 3 slices`.

Their test steps read under 40 s on at least four of six shards, so they mostly replayed the cache that the push run on the same commit saved. Three more log reads, cut short above the table, are not counted.
- **The dispatch's main-run floor holds.** Six main runs executed most of their packages: 2 scheduled (37927365187, 37934353580) and 4 push (37934058408, 37938584496, 37946464515, 37953570203). That is at least the 5 required. Push runs are affected-set runs by design, but these four executed 63–70 packages. Counting the hourly scheduled runs alone gives 2; see Acceptance notes.

## Why 40 and not 35

Two measured rules set the value, and the larger answer wins.

1. **Wall margin**, the 80% that the in-tree revert condition uses. The slowest job, 27.08 min, must be within 80% of the wall.

   | wall | 80% | jobs over it (of 396) |
   |--:|--:|--:|
   | 30 | 24.0 | 17 (15 pull_request, 2 merge_group) |
   | 35 | 28.0 | 0 |
   | 40 | 32.0 | 0 |

   On this rule alone, 35 qualifies, with 55 s to spare.

2. **The stall guard must speak first.** The comment above the value calls the stall guard "the primary detector … and fires well before this". I re-took the guard's measured headroom on the same 396 jobs with `node scripts/measure-stall-guard-headroom.mjs --from` over the window's saved jobs payloads. The 35 and 40 rows are scratch workflow copies read through `--root`; the 40 row was re-taken on this branch's tree.
   - The slowest observation is that same job. "Run this shard's tests" ends 26m38s after its job starts: p 6m59s plus s 19m39s.
   - The guard's window verdict lands 10 min later, and its cap-deferred verdict 20 min later.

   | `timeout-minutes` | window verdict (p+s+10m) | cap-deferred verdict (p+s+20m) | observations whose window verdict misses | observations whose deferred verdict misses |
   |--:|:--|:--|--:|--:|
   | 45 (today) | COVERED, 8m22s to spare | UNCOVERED by 1m38s | 0 | 8 |
   | **40** | **COVERED, 3m22s to spare** | UNCOVERED by 6m38s | **0** | 60 |
   | 35 | **UNCOVERED by 1m38s** | UNCOVERED by 11m38s | 8 | 151 |

At 35, the guard's main path could no longer deliver its verdict for a freeze late in the slowest shards; the job timeout would kill them first, unlabelled. 40 is the smallest whole-five value that keeps that path covered on every observation.

The cap-deferred path already misses at 45 on the 8 slowest observations, and it needs a wall of at least 47 min. So no value this re-size could pick restores it, and lowering the wall widens that gap; see Acceptance notes.

`check-stall-guard-budget` stays green at 40:
- Cap 20m, budget 40m, slack 20m on all three guarded `test` steps.
- `T − C = 20` is at least `W = 10`.
- No `--stall-minutes` or cap is touched.

## The comment

The structure is kept:
1. The backstop rationale paragraph, unchanged.
2. The raise history, now one line.
3. The re-size, with the window, counts, per-event maxima, the slowest run and the two rules above.
4. The revert-to-30 condition. Its 24-minute, every-scheduled-run-for-a-week text is unchanged. Its "It does not today" evidence is restated from this window. The reading instruction now names every shard and the stall-guard headroom.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, which computes the change set from the merge base `446c8b2a6`. It names 1 path and 47 commands. Each command ran at head `a549ca3a`, with its exit code written before any pipe.

- **42 exit 0.** This includes `pnpm check:stall-guard-budget`, `pnpm check:stall-guard-headroom` (`35 assertion(s) passed`), `pnpm check:required-contexts` (`7 required context name(s) pinned across 3 workflow(s)`), `pnpm check:workflow-step-name-quoting` and `pnpm check:nul-bytes`.
- **4 exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET.** These are `check:dts-closure`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure` and `check:sourcemap-no-sources-content`. Each loads every package's built `dist/`, and this diff touches no package. They are NOT MEASURED.
- **`pnpm check:pm-dispatch-gates`**, the long battery, ran detached with its exit code recorded. It is quoted in the report on the card.
- **Outside the derived list:**
  - `node scripts/check-stall-guard-budget.mjs` exits 0: `every effective cap clears its job budget by at least one stall window`.
  - `--list` exits 0, with the three `test` rows at budget 40m and slack 20m.
- **Families that take a value from the workflow** (`--verify-required-set`, `check-shard-attestation --emit/--verify`, `check-test-completeness`) are NOT MEASURED locally by construction. CI runs them.

No package and no published file is touched, so this PR carries `skip-changeset`.

## Acceptance notes

1. **The revert condition's population mostly replays (noted, not filed).** "Every scheduled run for a week" reads the hourly runs.
   - In this window, 3 of the 5 scheduled runs replayed most packages from the cache their commit's push run had saved. Their slowest jobs read 1.6, 14.0 and 11.4 min.
   - Over the same hours, pull_request runs read up to 27.1 min.
   - So the condition can read as met on light runs while PR and queue shards sit above 24 min. Whoever applies it should read pull_request and merge_group walls too, and the stall-guard headroom at 30.
   - The condition text is kept as dispatched.
2. **The deferred stall-guard path, today and after.** Lowering the wall moves the cap-deferred verdict out of reach on more runs: 8 of 396 test-step observations at 45, 60 at 40.
   - That path fires only when the source-side liveness probe sees a guarded group still writing, which means a buffering layer is hiding a live suite.
   - The same gap already exists at the current walls of `dogfood` "Boot example apps…" (needs 33m, has 30m) and `temporal-conformance` "non-SQL temporal backends…" (needs 31m, has 30m), per the same instrument at base.
   - Not in scope here; recorded so the trade is visible.
3. **What the commit message's "31-40 min" covers.** It is the band of the six heavy pre-change pull_request runs above (31.7–39.7). Round 2's 12-run sample read 20.5–39.1 min for the shard running the whole CLI. The tables above are the reading.
